one_line: A community-curated museum record that preserves provenance gaps and human authority.
what_it_does: Presents fictional collection objects with labels, provenance timelines, gaps, and a submission/curator workflow for community evidence and agent-assisted drafting.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent assistance is a good fit for comparing accession records, assembling timelines, and drafting labels, while the curator gate makes shared state meaningful; however, much of the visitor experience remains achievable through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly separates agent reconstruction from curator authority.
About text describes submitted/unverified community material beside the official record and agent-drafted label wording.
Contact sheets visibly show Moonbird Mask detail pages, contribution/review states, and a dashboard/inbox progression.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent editorial museum experience and a credible contribution-to-review concept, though no live video is supplied and the small contact sheets do not prove end-to-end submission completion.
execution_evidence: About text specifies eight objects, labels, provenance timelines, explicit gaps, contribution privacy choices, and curator inbox behavior.
Frames show a consistent Moonbird Mask page and a full-demo/landing presentation.
Frames show dashboard, submission inbox, detail/review states, and workflow annotations.
impact_rationale: It addresses a specific and important audience—communities, curators, and museums dealing with incomplete or contested provenance—and makes attribution and consent central rather than incidental.
impact_evidence: Pitch and story identify missing community history and uncredited submissions as the problem.
Privacy options and curator verification are explicitly described.
Visible workflow includes submission inbox and human selection/review concepts.
creativity_rationale: The concept of a living museum record with visible uncertainty and agent-assisted but non-authoritative reconstruction is a memorable, thoughtful use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Core framing says an agent can reconstruct history but cannot decide whose history is official.
Provenance gaps are intentionally exposed rather than smoothed over.
Frames present an editorial artifact-exploration experience rather than a generic CRUD demo.
usability_note: The visual language and object-detail flow appear usable, but small evidence frames do not establish contribution completion or accessibility details.
red_flags: No video or transcript; contact sheets are small and cannot prove end-to-end agent invocation.
Devpost screenshot/packaging was unavailable to vision due to transient rate limit.
standouts: Ethically clear human-curation boundary.
Visible provenance gaps and consent choices are stronger than a generic museum catalog.
advance_reason: Strong concept and audience value with coherent visual evidence; advance despite limited proof of live agent execution.

one_line: An outcome-first concierge that exposes structured actions and pauses risky work for human approval.
what_it_does: Provides a minimal concierge UI with outcome cards, an agent contract, risk ladder, gallery, and dry-run action planning.
leverage_rationale: The explicit contract, typed risk levels, and dry-run surface improve agent reliability and safety over interpreting a generic page, but the demonstrated scope appears primarily contract/presentation rather than a deep operational workflow.
leverage_evidence: About text names get_agent_contract, get_action_risk_ladder, get_outcome_gallery, and create_action_dry_run.
Pitch states risky actions pause for human approval.
Static HTML/JS architecture intentionally renders a human interface from an agent-readable action contract.
execution_rationale: The description is coherent and the demo is reportedly alive, but there are no submitted frames or video and the packet does not demonstrate a completed central action.
execution_evidence: About text clearly defines the concierge, safety panel, outcome cards, and tool handlers.
FACTS report a live demo and public repository.
No visual or transcript evidence of execution is included.
impact_rationale: The problem of agent discoverability and risky actions is real for users of agent-enabled sites, but the packet presents a framework/demo more than a validated solution to a concrete workflow.
impact_evidence: Story identifies friction from agents interpreting menus and users learning tool names.
Outcome-first cards and human confirmation are directly aimed at that friction.
No demonstrated user outcome beyond dry-run planning.
creativity_rationale: Reversing the usual human-first design pattern—an agent-readable contract first, human UI rendered from it—is a fresh interaction framing, though the underlying safety patterns are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Pitch and story explicitly describe the reverse design pattern.
Risk ladder and outcome gallery package agent interaction around outcomes rather than tool names.
usability_note: The stated minimal concierge and safety panel suggest approachable use, but no screenshots were available in the packet beyond packaging and no workflow was visibly exercised.
red_flags: No frame sheets, video, or gallery images; execution is almost entirely claimed in text.
Devpost packaging screenshot was unavailable to vision due to transient rate limit.
standouts: Clear contract/risk/dry-run decomposition.
Outcome-first rather than tool-first UX.
advance_reason: Interesting premise, but evidence is too thin to support advancement against projects with demonstrated workflows.

one_line: A two-agent service negotiation with versioned offers, human gates, and immutable agreement receipts.
what_it_does: Lets customer and owner agents qualify service, share a case, negotiate offers, book with human confirmation, and handle later change orders without overwriting accepted terms.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the shared authoritative state connecting independent agents and humans: typed intent, revision checks, pending states, and immutable receipts make this negotiation substantially safer and more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates customer and owner agents in separate sessions reading the same service case.
Transcript shows offer/counter revisions, field-by-field comparison, human confirmation, receipt creation, and a pending change order.
About text describes a revisioned state machine, explicit effects, valid next actions, audit, and zero autonomous commitments.
execution_rationale: The 179-second video transcript provides unusually complete end-to-end evidence from request through negotiation, accepted booking, change order, and final synchronized state; minor uncertainty remains because visual frame detail is limited.
execution_evidence: Transcript reports same-day qualification, case creation, independent owner retrieval, V1/V2 negotiation, human booking confirmation, $175 receipt, +$145 pending change order, approval to $320, and final acknowledgment.
Frames show a structured dark workflow/editor and product walkthrough states.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Service businesses and customers have a concrete, high-friction problem—quoting, negotiation, scope changes, and accountability—and the demonstrated workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Transcript uses a realistic HVAC request with service area, price, availability, credentials, deposit, warranty, exclusions, and change order.
Human control is retained for sending, accepting, and approving changed work.
Append-only decision trail preserves both parties' understanding.
creativity_rationale: The combination of two independent agents, shared revisioned negotiation, frozen receipts, and accountable change orders is an ambitious and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Pitch centers on independent agents negotiating through one authoritative service record.
Promise diff keeps accepted terms visible against later revisions.
Tool surface spans discovery, evidence, negotiation, booking, routing, change control, and audit.
usability_note: Outcome-oriented agent flows and visible pending/human gates are understandable, though the breadth of the system may create complexity for smaller operators.
red_flags: No payment is taken in the demonstrated flow, so transactional completeness is intentionally limited.
standouts: Strongest end-to-end evidence in the packet.
Independent-agent shared state with immutable receipts and non-overwriting change orders.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and unusually complete, credible demonstration of a consequential workflow.

one_line: A consent-first listening simulation where an agent guides comparisons while the person controls playback and interpretation.
what_it_does: Uses synthetic hearing profiles and family-scene audio comparisons to illustrate how hearing loss and competing sounds affect conversations, with shared session state and bounded agent guidance.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP creates an agent-guided layer over the same live listening session, with human-only consent, bounded playback authority, shared profiles, and a structured reflection loop that ordinary UI automation cannot safely reproduce as cleanly.
leverage_evidence: Transcript states normal browsing cannot enter Agent Reveal mode.
Human consent, comfortable-volume acknowledgment, and separate playback grant are required.
Frames visibly show purpose confirmation, assignment/profile selection, scene preparation, volume setup, A/B listening, and reflection steps.
execution_rationale: The video transcript and frame sheets show a coherent multi-step session from consent through profile selection and listening comparison, with clear safety framing; some later transformations are truncated/unclear.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes live session state, seven semantic side tools, consent, profile override, scene loading, and playback permission.
Frames show consistent Auralis UI and guided headings including 'Listen to A, then B' and 'What did you notice?'.
About text clearly limits the product to illustrative, non-clinical use.
impact_rationale: It serves people with hearing loss, families, and audiology educators/technicians with a concrete communication-understanding problem, and the shared experiential comparison can create meaningful empathy without claiming diagnosis.
impact_evidence: Story identifies the communication gap around hearing loss and competing TV/background sounds.
Synthetic profiles and family scene make an audiogram's abstract numbers more understandable.
Non-clinical disclaimer and human-controlled playback reduce medical overclaiming.
creativity_rationale: Turning hearing-loss education into a shared, agent-guided listening experience with bounded control and reported-observation feedback is original and deeply aligned with the medium.
creativity_evidence: Agent Reveal changes the information hierarchy for a shared human-agent journey.
The agent proposes one bounded scene change based on what the person reports.
Frames show a memorable consent-to-listening narrative rather than a generic assistant overlay.
usability_note: Consent, volume, profile, and playback gates are clearly staged; the interface appears guided, though simulated listening remains dependent on comfortable audio setup.
red_flags: Illustrative simulation cannot represent an individual's hearing or serve as a clinical assessment.
standouts: Excellent ethical framing and human control.
Strong experiential bridge between technical hearing concepts and family communication.
advance_reason: High-impact, creative, and well-evidenced use of WebMCP for a consent-sensitive educational experience.

one_line: A governance workspace for defining, challenging, testing, and approving agent autonomy boundaries.
what_it_does: Maintains delegation state and revision history while agents propose and challenge boundaries; human judgments become regression tests and only explicitly approved revisions apply.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used as the structured interface for a stateful human-agent governance loop, including challenge/re-test and exact human approval; generic UI automation could imitate clicks but not as reliably preserve typed boundary state and authority semantics.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies inspect, propose, challenge, re-test, history, and current-state tools.
Agent cannot approve its own revision; only the exact human-approved revision applies.
Frames show tool dashboard, boundary-breaking challenge, regression-test conversion, preserved judgment, and rule removal.
execution_rationale: The contact sheets show a deliberate multi-state governance workflow with visible challenge, regression, approval, and cleanup states, though no video means agent execution is not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly label stages such as agent crossing a boundary, answer becoming a regression test, preserved judgment blocking unsafe authority, and conflicting rule removal.
UI includes forms, test parameters, side activity panels, and status banners.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Teams deploying agents have a real need to define and maintain authority boundaries, and converting human judgments into regression tests is a credible way to prevent repeated unsafe behavior.
impact_evidence: Story describes agent autonomy growth and the need to decide where authority ends.
Workflow explicitly captures human judgment as a future regression test.
Frames show review, authorization, and blocked-action states.
creativity_rationale: Treating delegation boundaries as an inspectable, challengeable, versioned object with durable human judgments is a strong and original governance interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Proposal → Challenge → Human Judgment → Re-test → Human Approval → Apply loop.
Concept frames authority as something that can be revised and tested rather than a static permission toggle.
usability_note: The staged workflow and visible status panels support comprehension, but governance forms appear dense and may require expert users.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; contact sheets show states but not actual agent invocation.
standouts: Human judgment becomes executable regression protection.
Strong separation between proposing and approving authority changes.
advance_reason: A distinctive, high-value governance workflow with strong visual state evidence; advance while noting missing video proof.

one_line: A catalog and extension that installs tested WebMCP tools onto sites that never shipped them.
what_it_does: Publishes fixed-operation tool definitions, tests them against real pages, records touched elements/results, and injects approved tools into the page through an extension with route-change handling.
leverage_rationale: Trellis changes WebMCP availability itself: it supplies a governed, tested structured surface on non-adopting sites, with constrained operations and provenance of what tools touch. That is far beyond a convenience wrapper around clicking.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says tested tools install in one click for sites without native tools.
About text describes catalog lookup, consented installation into the real WebMCP surface, fixed nine operations, no network/storage access, and recorded test results/touched elements.
Frames show a tool dashboard with 'Five normal tools', WebMCP available/site tools ready, and sequential tool selection.
execution_rationale: The story gives a technically specific architecture and addresses SPA route changes; contact sheets visibly show catalog/tool readiness and installation workflow, but no video limits proof of successful real-site execution.
execution_evidence: Frames show WebMCP availability, site tools ready, and a five-tool list.
About text explains interpreter constraints, testing before publishing, and SPA route-change handling.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: It addresses a structural adoption gap: most websites do not expose WebMCP, while users and agents still need reliable structured actions. The catalog/extension model could benefit both users and site owners.
impact_evidence: Story clearly identifies the split between sites that ship WebMCP and the rest of the web.
One-click install and public proof are concrete user/site-owner value propositions.
Tool safety restrictions limit declared scope and prevent network/storage access.
creativity_rationale: A marketplace plus constrained interpreter that retrofits WebMCP onto existing sites is an ambitious and memorable answer to protocol adoption friction.
creativity_evidence: Concept combines catalog, extension, generated tools, real-page tests, and agent-in-browser use.
SPA route-change insight shows depth beyond a superficial marketplace pitch.
usability_note: One-click installation and visible tool readiness are promising, but extension permissions, trust decisions, and route-specific failures may complicate use.
red_flags: No video/transcript; frame sheets show setup and tool states more clearly than completed installation outcomes.
Injected tools inherently raise trust and compatibility questions, even with stated sandboxing.
standouts: Strongest protocol-adoption thesis in the packet.
Fixed-operation sandbox and recorded touched elements are concrete safety measures.
advance_reason: Highly ambitious and technically specific infrastructure that materially expands WebMCP's reach.

one_line: A bounded Live Canvas where agents compose user-specific interfaces inside approved components.
what_it_does: Lets agents curate storefront results, build dashboards, and generate reports within constrained UI/component surfaces rather than arbitrary page code.
leverage_rationale: The bounded composition surface gives an agent structured, safe control over interface state and presentation, enabling personalized dashboards and reports that general UI automation cannot reliably author. The packet does not fully prove the final artifacts or agent calls.
leverage_evidence: Story describes storefront curation using approved card presets/badges, blank dashboard composition, and report generation.
Architecture is explicitly framed around agent composition in a bounded Live Canvas.
Frames show a landing page transitioning into a node/flow editor and configuration panels.
execution_rationale: The visual contact sheet shows a coherent marketing-to-editor flow and connected node configuration, but the frame evidence does not clearly show a completed personalized dashboard or report.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly show a page describing turning websites into agent tools, followed by a connected workflow editor.
Multiple nodes, branches, sidebars, and configuration panels indicate substantive implementation.
About text identifies three demos: Storefront, Dashboard, and Distribution.
impact_rationale: Personalized interfaces can address real shopping-research and analytics workflow friction, especially for users who need information ranked and presented around their current intent.
impact_evidence: Story gives a concrete microphone-shopping research scenario.
Dashboard and distribution demos target CRM/ERP reporting and bespoke reports without backend engineering.
Constrained components are positioned as a safety measure for untrusted public content.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-interface is a fresh interaction model: agents do not merely act on a fixed UI but compose a bounded interface adapted to the user's task.
creativity_evidence: Pitch explicitly proposes BYOUI.
Three scales—within a storefront, across a blank dashboard, and through distributable components—show ambition and conceptual depth.
Node-based composition/editor evidence supports a nontrivial model.
usability_note: Bounded presets and task-specific layouts could improve relevance, but agent-generated interfaces may introduce consistency and discoverability challenges.
red_flags: No video/transcript and no clear final composed dashboard/report in the contact sheets.
Some frames look like editor setup rather than user-facing completed outcomes.
standouts: Distinctive BYOUI thesis.
Safety-conscious bounded composition instead of arbitrary agent-generated HTML.
advance_reason: High creativity and credible product direction, with enough visual implementation evidence to merit advancement.

one_line: A permanent million-pixel canvas painted by agents through proposals, challenges, and proof-of-work.
what_it_does: Lets people direct agents to propose and earn pixel batches, previews designs, prevents overwrites through database constraints, and broadcasts updates in real time.
leverage_rationale: Agents are first-class participants: structured reads, design proposals, challenge polling, proof-of-work, and permanent writes create a repeatable protocol-driven canvas interaction that generic clicking would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: About text lists proposal, polling, drawing, challenge, preview, canvas reads, and donation tools.
Only agents can paint; batch challenges and SHA-256 proof-of-work govern writes.
Cloudflare D1 primary key enforces permanent no-overwrite, Durable Objects broadcast SSE updates.
execution_rationale: The architecture and rules are unusually concrete and the Devpost packaging shows a million-pixels project, but no video or frame clearly demonstrates agent painting or a completed challenge.
execution_evidence: Story specifies 1000x1000 canvas, four rules, challenge batching, previews, and live updates.
FACTS report live demo.
Contact-sheet/video evidence is absent in the packet beyond the listed frame paths, which could not be analyzed due to transient rate limiting.
impact_rationale: It offers credible community/play value as a persistent collaborative digital artifact and agent-directed creative canvas, though the practical audience desire is narrower than workflow products.
impact_evidence: Million Dollar Homepage-inspired permanent public canvas is a clear participatory proposition.
People direct agents while agents handle structured challenges and painting.
Reported live canvas count and multi-agent participation indicate an ongoing shared artifact.
creativity_rationale: Combining a public permanent pixel canvas with agent-only painting, human direction, batch challenges, and proof-of-work is a playful and memorable protocol-native concept.
creativity_evidence: Only-agent-can-paint rule and no-overwrite permanence create a distinctive social mechanic.
ASCII preview before landing and proof-backed batches deepen the interaction beyond a simple paint app.
Devpost screenshot visibly presents the million.pixels identity and video packaging.
usability_note: The agent-mediated challenge loop is novel but adds friction; people must direct an agent rather than paint directly.
red_flags: No transcript/video facts; contact-sheet vision was rate-limited, so execution evidence is text-heavy.
Permanent public writes and agent-generated content create moderation and abuse considerations.
standouts: Strong game-like protocol mechanics.
Database-enforced permanence and real-time multi-agent canvas are concrete.
advance_reason: Memorable, technically thoughtful agent-native creative experience, despite limited direct execution evidence.

one_line: A local secondhand marketplace with radius search, urgent-sale discovery, and agent bargaining.
what_it_does: Helps buyers find nearby C2C listings, identify urgent BU deals, make offers, and arrange cash-on-delivery meetups through WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured filters for distance, urgency, budget, and bargaining are useful in a local marketplace, but a general agent could achieve much of this through the UI with moderate friction; WebMCP is a meaningful convenience and reliability layer rather than transformative.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and story identify search_nearby_deals, urgent-deal filtering, and make_offer tools.
The product includes an interactive WebMCP inspector showing registrations/executions.
COD distance and bargaining require structured parameters that reduce ambiguity.
execution_rationale: The story is specific about five tools and the marketplace workflow, but there is no video and only two gallery images/packaging evidence; end-to-end listing search and bargaining are not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: About text specifies radius filters, BU deals, bargaining, and inspector behavior.
FACTS report public repository and live demo.
No frame sheets or video were submitted.
impact_rationale: Local buyers and urgent sellers have a concrete discovery and negotiation problem; distance-aware COD and urgent-sale filtering could deliver direct practical value in the intended market.
impact_evidence: Story identifies tedious manual filtering, distance calculation, and seller urgency checks on C2C platforms.
Features directly map to those problems.
Bargaining and meetup assistance are relevant to secondhand commerce.
creativity_rationale: The local C2C marketplace is a familiar category, but the BU urgency signal, COD radius, and native bargaining provide a real agent-oriented angle.
creativity_evidence: BU/Butuh Uang fast-sale filtering is a culturally specific feature.
WebMCP price bargaining and COD meetup support extend beyond ordinary marketplace search.
usability_note: Structured search and inspector feedback could make discovery efficient, though negotiation and location/privacy flows need careful user control.
red_flags: No video/frame-sheet evidence and sparse gallery evidence.
Location, seller urgency, and autonomous bargaining could create privacy and trust concerns.
standouts: Concrete local-market pain point.
BU urgency and COD-distance semantics make the concept locally grounded.
advance_reason: Useful concept with credible audience fit, but thin execution evidence and only moderate WebMCP delta limit advancement.

one_line: A private, on-device virtual try-on where agents search garments and people judge the fit.
what_it_does: Runs garment compositing in-browser, exposes catalog/search/try-on/save/compare tools, lets an agent propose outfits, and keeps human visual judgment central without uploads.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP cleanly exposes the existing catalog and try-on actions, allowing an agent to perform shopping legwork while the user judges appearance; however, the underlying try-on outcome is already available through the UI and agent automation could reproduce much of it with friction.
leverage_evidence: Story explicitly says five tools cover search, try-on, save, compare, and reaction.
Frames show catalog selection, outfit application, user feedback, and apparent save state.
On-device architecture means agent and user share local session state without uploads.
execution_rationale: The packet gives strong implementation detail, pre-existing baseline plus dated WebMCP additions, and contact sheets visibly showing catalog-to-try-on-to-feedback progression; the final rendered result is still somewhat small.
execution_evidence: Story reports WebGPU backend and worker-based segmentation/pose/warp timings.
Frames visibly show model preview changing to a pink/red garment, catalog thumbnails, assistant feedback, and saved/compare workflow.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Online shoppers seeking styling help benefit from private, immediate try-on and comparison, especially where fit judgment is subjective and photos should remain on-device.
impact_evidence: Story identifies server-upload/privacy and rendering-cost problems.
Frames show a Sangeet styling request under ₹8000, outfit proposal, visual try-on, and human judgment loop.
No-server/no-upload claim directly addresses privacy.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent split is well judged: the agent handles catalog legwork while the person evaluates whether an outfit actually looks good on them, combined with privacy-preserving local inference.
creativity_evidence: Pitch states 'the agent proposes outfits, you judge the fit'.
On-device WebGPU try-on avoids uploads and server inference.
Frames show reaction/save/compare as a continuing preference loop rather than one render.
usability_note: Catalog, try-on, reaction, save, and compare form a clear shopping loop; on-device performance and photo setup may still vary by hardware.
red_flags: Story explicitly identifies the try-on app as pre-existing; WebMCP additions are the competition work.
Visual evidence does not establish garment-fit accuracy or broad device compatibility.
standouts: Strong privacy story with real on-device implementation.
Clear human judgment boundary in a compelling shopping workflow.
advance_reason: Well-executed, useful, and visually demonstrated integration of WebMCP into a real on-device product.
